transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I really don't want to waste your time because it's probably not a huge deal, but... I've just been having this kind of constant restless feeling? 

It's like I'm wound a little too tight, I guess, and I just can't fully settle down. Even when I'm supposed to be calmly sitting through a planning meeting at work—I'm a retail buyer, so we have a lot of those—or even when I'm trying to do something relaxing on my own, like painting or doing yoga. I just can't seem to completely relax my body. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I hope I'm explaining it okay.

When you feel this wound-up, restless feeling, is your mind also racing with worries about things—like work, health, finances, or other concerns—or is it more just a physical sensation in your body that you can't settle?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say it's worries. I hope that's okay to say. I mean, I'm actually a pretty positive person, usually! I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around stressing out about my health or money or anything like that. I try to keep a pretty good perspective on those things. 

So my mind isn't really racing with bad thoughts or anxieties... it's really just that physical feeling. Just this sort of... little hum in my body that wants to keep going when I know I should just be sitting still. It's honestly not a huge deal, just a little annoying sometimes. 

Does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

When you describe this 'hum' in your body that wants to keep going—does that mean you find yourself fidgeting a lot, like tapping your feet or fingers, or moving around, even when you're trying to sit still? Or is it more of an internal feeling of tension without much visible movement?

Well, um... I guess it is a little bit visible. I really hope this doesn't make me sound unprofessional, because I take my job very seriously and I really do pay attention! But... yeah, I suppose I do fidget a little. 

It's not a huge distraction or anything, but, like, when I'm on calls with suppliers, my foot is usually bouncing under the desk. And I'll find myself clicking a pen or twisting my ring around. It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but sometimes I do it so much that I have to make sure to mute myself so they don't hear the clicking. Or I'll kind of purposely move my hands out of the camera view so no one sees me messing with my jewelry. I just really don't want anyone to think I'm being rude or ignoring them, you know? 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope that's helpful, and not too silly of an example.

Going back to when you were a child or teenager—did you have similar experiences with fidgeting, restlessness, or difficulty sitting still back then, or is this something that's more recently started to bother you?

Oh, um... wow, going back that far... I guess, well, I hope this doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid, because I really did try to be good and I loved school! But, um, yes, I suppose it's been there for a long time. 

I actually remember in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes send notes home to my parents. It wasn't because I was being mean or anything like that! I just... I had a lot of energy, I guess. I would sort of pop out of my seat a lot, or I'd get so excited about what we were learning that I'd accidentally talk over my classmates. And, um, I was always rushing to answer questions before the teacher even finished asking them. I just wanted to participate so badly, you know? 

I really hope that doesn't sound too awful. I always meant well! Does that answer your question okay?

When you're working on a task that requires focus—like reviewing supplier contracts or planning a buyer's order—do you find it hard to keep your attention on it, or do you tend to get distracted and jump between things?

Oh, um... no, actually! I hope it's alright to say no to that one. I really don't have much trouble with the focus part. I take my work very seriously, and I'd hate for you to think I'm making mistakes on contracts or buyer orders, because I'm actually very thorough! 

So, um, when I need to sit down and review something important, I can definitely keep my attention on it. I might be, you know, bouncing my foot under the desk like I mentioned before, but my mind is completely on the task. I don't really jump around or lose track of what I'm doing. 

Is... is that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, and I really don't want to sound like I'm doing a bad job at work!

From elementary school all the way through to now as an adult, would you say this restless feeling and fidgeting has been pretty much constant throughout your life, or have there been longer stretches of time—maybe weeks, months, or years—where it went away or was much less noticeable?

Well, um... I guess it's always been there in the background, like I mentioned with the school notes and all. I've always been a bit of a fidgeter, and I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I haven't tried to improve myself! I've always managed it pretty well, I think. 

But, um... to be completely honest—and I hope this is okay to share, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my family—it has been a little bit harder to manage lately. Maybe for the last... two years and a couple of months? 

My husband and I have been dealing with some conflicts with my in-laws, and it's just been taking over a lot of our evenings. It's been a little stressful, and I guess I've noticed that restless feeling bubbling up a bit more since all of that started. I really try not to let it show, but it's just been a bit more noticeable to me. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not oversharing about my personal life, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right!

You mentioned you can focus well on important work tasks like contracts. But in your everyday life—like when you're reading a book, watching a movie, or having a casual conversation—do you find yourself having trouble keeping your attention, or does your mind wander off even when you're trying to listen?

Oh, um... well, I hope this doesn't make me sound like a bad listener, because I really do try to pay attention to people! I think I'm usually pretty engaged, especially with things I enjoy. But... I suppose, occasionally... I do have these little moments where my mind sort of slips away. 

Like, um, sometimes in sourcing meetings at work, or even just sitting at the dinner table with my husband... I can be looking right at someone, and they'll ask me a question, and then a few seconds later I realize I only caught the very last part of what they said. And then I have to ask them to repeat it, which is always so embarrassing! I always feel terrible when it happens, I promise I'm not ignoring them on purpose. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound rude or dismissive. I really do care about what people are saying! Does that sound like what you're asking about?

When you have those moments where your mind slips away during meetings or conversations, how often would you say that happens—is it just every now and then, or is it something that happens pretty regularly throughout your day?

Oh, um... it's really not that often! I'd hate for you to think I'm just sitting there spacing out all day. I really do try my best to be present. 

It's just... maybe every now and then? Like I said, it's usually just in those sourcing meetings, or sometimes at the dinner table. I'll be looking right at my husband, and he'll ask me something, and... well, like I mentioned, a few seconds later I'll realize I only caught the tail end of it. And then I have to ask him to repeat himself. 

But I promise it's not a regular, all-the-time thing! It's just a little slip every once in a while. I hope that's okay? I really don't want it to sound worse than it is, because I do value what people are saying to me!

Besides those occasional moments where your mind slips away in meetings, do you find yourself having trouble with things like keeping track of your belongings, organizing your tasks or schedule, or remembering to do things you've planned to do?

Oh, um... goodness, no. I really hope I haven't made it sound like I'm completely scatterbrained! I'm actually very careful about all of that. With my work as a buyer, I really have to stay on top of things, so I'm always very organized with my schedules and my to-do lists. 

I don't really ever lose my belongings or forget what I've planned for the day. I actually take a lot of pride in being responsible and keeping everything running smoothly, both at work and at home. I always make sure everything is right where it belongs.

Is it okay that I don't struggle with those things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being a helpful patient!

You mentioned that you can focus well on important work tasks, and you're very organized with your schedule. But thinking more broadly—when you're doing things that aren't as interesting or engaging to you, like routine paperwork, household chores, or less stimulating activities—do you find it harder to keep your attention on those, or do you still manage pretty well?

Oh, um... no, I actually manage those things just fine! I hope that's okay? I'd really hate for you to think I'm neglecting my responsibilities or letting my house get messy or anything like that. 

Even with the really routine paperwork at the office, or, you know, just doing the dishes and laundry at home... I just push through and get it done. Being a buyer means I really can't let the boring details slide, so I've always made sure to stay on top of them, even if it's not the most exciting part of my day. I really try my best to be dependable! 

Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers for your assessment. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult by not having a problem with that!

When you're at home in the evening and trying to relax—maybe reading, watching TV, or doing a hobby like the painting you mentioned earlier—do you find it easier to keep your attention on those things compared to work, or do you still have those moments where your mind drifts away?

Oh, um, when I'm relaxing? I... I don't really have any trouble then either. I hope I'm not sounding like a broken record or being unhelpful by saying no again! 

When I sit down to paint in the evening, or if my husband and I are just watching a show, I'm perfectly fine. I can just settle in and enjoy it. My mind doesn't really wander off when I'm doing things I like, and I really do try to just be present and unwind after a long day at work. 

I'm sorry if I'm not giving you very many examples of my mind drifting! I just want to make sure I'm painting an accurate picture for you. Is it alright that I don't really struggle with focusing when I'm relaxing?

When you have those moments where your mind slips away during meetings or conversations with your husband, how much does that actually interfere with your ability to do your job well or affect your relationships? Does it cause you real problems, or is it more of just a minor annoyance?

Oh, um... well, it's... I mean, I really don't want it to sound like I'm doing a bad job or anything! I try so, so hard to be good at what I do. But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it has caused a few little hiccups. 

At work, there have been a couple of times where I had to, you know, correct some purchase orders because I missed a detail when my mind wandered. And my planning coordinator has started doing some extra reviews of my work. But it's just to be safe! I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I still get everything done! 

And at home... well, sometimes family dinners get a little... tense. I guess I tend to jump in and talk over people because I'm so eager to share, or I just can't sit still and wait my turn. My husband and kids get a little frustrated with me. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I don't mean to be rude or disruptive! 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I really hope I'm not coming across as a difficult person to work with or live with. I just want to be helpful and answer your questions properly!

You mentioned that your mind occasionally slips away during meetings or conversations with your husband, and that you sometimes miss details in purchase orders. Over the past two years or so, how many times per week would you say these kinds of moments—where your mind drifts and you miss what someone is saying or what you're supposed to be paying attention to—actually happen to you?

Oh, um... well, as for how many times a week... I... I really don't want you to think I'm completely checked out or not trying my hardest! I really do try to listen, I promise. But, um... I guess it happens... maybe a few times a week? Is that a normal amount? I hope it's not too terrible. 

It's just that, sometimes... well, like in sourcing meetings at work, or even just sitting at the dinner table with my family... I can be looking right at someone, right in their eyes, and they'll ask me something. And then, a few seconds later, I just... I realize I only caught the very last part of what they said. And I have to ask them to repeat it. 

I feel so awful when it happens, I really do! I always apologize and try to make sure they know I care about what they're saying. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad listener or a bad wife. I'm really trying my best to stay focused! Does that answer your question okay?

When you say your mind slips away a few times a week during meetings or conversations—are those the only times during your day when you lose focus, or does it happen in other situations too, like when you're working on your buyer orders, managing your to-do lists, or doing other tasks throughout the day?

Oh, um... well, it's mostly just during those meetings and conversations. I really do try to stay on top of everything else! I have my to-do lists and I work so hard to keep everything organized. I don't want you to think my whole day is just me losing focus, because it's not, I promise!

But, um... I guess... if I'm thinking about the buyer orders and things like that... well, over the past couple of years, there have been a few little things. Like, I'll be absolutely sure I've checked a vendor spreadsheet so carefully—I really do try to be thorough!—but then our planning coordinator will catch a tiny mistake. Like maybe I transposed a SKU number, or I didn't notice a freight surcharge, or I accidentally carried the wrong quantity over into the final purchase order. 

It's just little things like that! And like I said before, my coordinator reviews it, so everything gets fixed and the orders go out perfectly fine. I just... I get a little embarrassed when she points it out, because I want to do a good job. I hope that doesn't make me sound careless. I really do care about getting the details right! Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant?

You mentioned that you sometimes miss details in your buyer orders and have those moments where your mind slips away in meetings a few times a week. But when you're doing something that's really important or has high stakes—like reviewing a major contract or handling a critical supplier issue—do you find it easier to keep your attention focused on that, or do you still have those same moments where your mind drifts?

Oh, goodness... um... well, when it's something really big, like a major contract, I definitely try extra, extra hard! I know how important those are, and I'd never want to let my company down or mess up a critical supplier relationship. I take those high-stakes things very seriously, I promise! 

But, um... as for whether it's actually easier to keep my attention focused then, or if my mind still slips away... I'm honestly not too sure? I haven't really noticed if there's a difference, to be perfectly honest. I just know I put a lot of pressure on myself to get the big things right, so I'm usually just pushing through as best I can. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry I don't have a more specific answer for you on that one... I just haven't really tracked it like that. Am I still giving you the right kind of information? I really want to be helpful!
